subject: maths
title: Measuring Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Year 3 Measuring Worksheets: Length, Mass and Capacity with Rulers, Scales and Jugs (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Measure, compare, add and subtract: lengths (m/cm/mm); mass (kg/g); volume/capacity (l/ml).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on measuring: lengths in m, cm and mm with a ruler, mass in kg and g on scales, capacity in l and ml in jugs, comparing mixed units such as 1 m 5 cm and 150 cm, and adding and subtracting measures in word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Start at 0, find what one mark is worth, and use the same unit to compare.
key_sub: 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g and 1 l = 1,000 ml. So 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm, which is shorter than 150 cm.
body_html:
What we measure

Length is how long something is. Mass is how heavy it is. Capacity is how much a container holds. Each one has its own units.

MeasureUnitsFacts
Lengthmillimetres (mm), centimetres (cm), metres (m)1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm
Massgrams (g), kilograms (kg)1 kg = 1,000 g
Capacitymillilitres (ml), litres (l)1 l = 1,000 ml

Measure with a ruler

Line up the end of the object with 0, not with the edge of the ruler and not with 1. Read the number at the other end.

If the object does not start at 0, take away the start from the end.

Read a scale or a jug

Not every mark has a number. First work out what one mark is worth: the jump between two numbers ÷ the number of spaces. Then count on from the number before.

Compare and order

To compare, change both measures to the same unit first.

Which is longer?

1 m 5 cm or 150 cm?

1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m 5 cm = 100 + 5 = 105 cm. 105 cm is less than 150 cm.

Answer: 150 cm is longer

Add and subtract

Add or subtract like units: metres with metres, centimetres with centimetres. If you make 100 cm, exchange it for 1 m. If you make 1,000 g, exchange it for 1 kg.

Adding mixed units

1 m 40 cm + 80 cm

40 cm + 80 cm = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm. 1 m + 1 m 20 cm = 2 m 20 cm.

Answer: 2 m 20 cm

Subtracting from 1 kg

1 kg − 350 g

1 kg = 1,000 g. 1,000 − 350 = 650.

Answer: 650 g

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting at 1 or at the edge of the rulerStart at 0, or take away the start from the end
Counting every mark on a scale as 1 or 10Work out what one mark is worth first
1 m 5 cm = 15 cm or 150 cm1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm
Thinking 1 kg is less than 900 g1 kg = 1,000 g, which is more than 900 g
1 m 40 cm + 80 cm = 1 m 120 cmExchange 100 cm for 1 m: 1 m 120 cm = 2 m 20 cm

faq.q: What measurement do Year 3 children learn?
faq.a: Year 3 pupils measure, compare, add and subtract lengths in m, cm and mm, mass in kg and g, and capacity in l and ml. They use rulers, weighing scales and measuring jugs.

faq.q: How do you measure with a ruler in Year 3?
faq.a: Line up one end of the object with 0 on the ruler, not with 1 or the edge. Read the number at the other end. Each small mark is 1 mm, and 10 mm make 1 cm.

faq.q: How do you read a scale when not every mark has a number?
faq.a: Find two numbers next to each other and count the spaces between them. Divide the jump by the spaces to find what one mark is worth, then count on from the number before the needle.

faq.q: Is 1 m 5 cm the same as 150 cm?
faq.a: No. 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm. 150 cm is the same as 1 m 50 cm.

sets.title: Measure length with a ruler: cm and mm

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
items.e: Look at a ruler. There are 10 small spaces in each centimetre. So 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: A metre stick has 100 centimetres marked on it. So 1 m = 100 cm.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of an ant?
items.e: An ant is tiny, shorter than 1 cm. Use millimetres for very short things.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil fits on a ruler. Use centimetres. Metres are for long things like a room.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of the playground?
items.e: The playground is long. Use metres. Kilograms measure mass, not length.
The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. So it is 7 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. So it is 5 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The rubber starts at 0 and ends at 4. So it is 4 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The piece of ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 8. So it is 8 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The pencil starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 2 = 7, so it is 7 cm long. You can also count the big spaces: there are 7.
The crayon starts at 1, not at 0. It ends at 6. 6 − 1 = 5, so it is 5 cm long. You can also count the big spaces: there are 5.
The rubber starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 7. 7 − 3 = 4, so it is 4 cm long. You can also count the big spaces: there are 4.
The piece of ribbon starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 8. 8 − 2 = 6, so it is 6 cm long. You can also count the big spaces: there are 6.
The crayon goes past 4 cm and then 6 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 4 cm 6 mm long.
The pencil goes past 6 cm and then 3 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 6 cm 3 mm long.
The rubber goes past 3 cm and then 8 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 3 cm 8 mm long.
The rubber is 3 cm and 5 mm long. 3 cm = 30 mm, and 30 + 5 = 35. So it is 35 mm long.
The pencil starts at 2 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm 4 mm. Take away 2 cm: 7 cm 4 mm − 2 cm = 5 cm 4 mm.
The crayon starts at 3 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm 8 mm. Take away 3 cm: 7 cm 8 mm − 3 cm = 4 cm 8 mm.

items.q: A worm is 6 cm 4 mm long. How long is it in millimetres?
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 cm = 60 mm. 60 + 4 = 64. The worm is 64 mm long.

sets.title: Read scales: mass in g and kg

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000. So 1 kg = 1,000 g.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram. 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of an apple?
items.e: An apple is light, about 100 grams. 100 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a Year 3 child?
items.e: A Year 3 child is about 25 kilograms. 25 g is lighter than a bar of chocolate.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of carrots. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 300: 300 + 50 = 350 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of an apple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 100: 100 + 50 = 150 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a jar of honey. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 400: 400 + 50 = 450 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 200: 200 + 100 = 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 100 = 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of apples. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 800: 800 + 100 = 900 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a loaf of bread. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 500: 500 + 300 = 800 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a box of cereal. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 0: 400 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 2 kg: 2 kg + 500 g = 2 kg 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 1 kg: 1 kg + 500 g = 1 kg 500 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 300 g = 1 kg 300 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 7 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg + 700 g = 2 kg 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 6 kg: 6 kg + 1 kg = 7 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pile of books. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 2 kg: 2 kg + 1 kg = 3 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of flour. How much more flour is needed to make 1 kg?
items.e: The needle is at 600 g. 1 kg = 1,000 g. 1,000 − 600 = 400 g more.

items.q: The scale shows a bowl of cherries. The empty bowl weighs 100 g. What is the mass of the cherries?
items.e: Each mark is 50 g, so the needle is at 250 g. Take away the bowl: 250 − 100 = 150 g.

sets.title: Read jugs: capacity in ml and l

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. So 1 l = 1,000 ml.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a teaspoon holds?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 millilitres. 5 l would fill a big bucket halfway.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a mug holds?
items.e: A mug of tea is about 300 millilitres. 300 l would fill a bath.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a bucket holds?
items.e: A bucket holds about 10 litres. 10 ml is only two teaspoons.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 ml. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 50 = 250 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 ml. The water is 1 line above 300: 300 + 50 = 350 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 ml. The water is 1 line above 400: 400 + 50 = 450 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 ml. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 100 = 300 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 ml. The water is 1 line above 600: 600 + 100 = 700 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 ml. The water is 1 line above 800: 800 + 100 = 900 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 ml. The water is 3 lines above 250: 250 + 150 = 400 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 ml. The water is 3 lines above 500: 500 + 150 = 650 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 ml. The water is 1 line above 500: 500 + 50 = 550 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 ml. The water is 2 lines above 750: 750 + 100 = 850 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 ml. The water is 3 lines above 1 l: 1 l + 300 ml = 1 l 300 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 ml. The water is 2 lines above 1 l 500 ml: 1 l 500 ml + 200 ml = 1 l 700 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 l = 1,000 ml, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 ml. The water is 1 line above 3 l: 3 l + 500 ml = 3 l 500 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 l = 1,000 ml, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 ml. The water is 1 line above 1 l: 1 l + 500 ml = 1 l 500 ml.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 500 ml?
items.e: Each line is 50 ml, so the water is at 150 ml. 500 − 150 = 350 ml more.

items.q: Jack pours 250 ml of water out of the jug. How much is left?
items.e: The water is at 800 ml. Water is poured out, so subtract: 800 − 250 = 550 ml.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 m 5 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Add the 5 cm: 100 + 5 = 105 cm. It is not 15 cm, and it is not 150 cm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 m 50 cm = ☐ cm
Find the missing number. 2 m 30 cm = ☐ cm
Find the missing number. 4 cm 5 mm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 4 cm = 40 mm. Add the 5 mm: 40 + 5 = 45 mm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 kg 200 g = ☐ g
Find the missing number. 1 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Add the 50 g: 1,000 + 50 = 1,050 g. The 5 is in the tens place.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 l 500 ml = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Add the 500 ml: 1,000 + 500 = 1,500 ml. 600 ml would mean 1 l = 100 ml.

items.q: Which is the same as 320 cm?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so 300 cm = 3 m. 320 cm = 3 m and 20 cm left over.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm, 1 m 40 cm = 140 cm. So the answer is 150 cm.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2 m = 200 cm, 2 m 5 cm = 205 cm, 1 m 95 cm = 195 cm. So the answer is 190 cm.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g. So the answer is 1 kg 50 g.

items.q: Which is the lightest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 kg 20 g = 1,020 g. So the answer is 600 g.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 l = 1,000 ml, 1 l 200 ml = 1,200 ml. So the answer is 1 l 200 ml.

items.q: Which holds the least?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 2 l = 2,000 ml, 1 l 900 ml = 1,900 ml, 2 l 50 ml = 2,050 ml. So the answer is 1 l 900 ml.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 m 5 cm = 100 cm + 5 cm = 105 cm. 105 cm is less than 150 cm.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. 1,000 g is more than 900 g. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 900.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 3 l = 3,000 ml and 2 l 900 ml = 2,900 ml. 3,000 is more than 2,900.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 4 cm = 40 mm. 4 cm is more than 30 mm.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: Change them to centimetres: 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm. 95 < 105 < 150.

items.q: Which list goes from the lightest to the heaviest?
items.e: Change them to grams: 1 kg = 1,000 g and 1 kg 200 g = 1,200 g. 800 < 1,000 < 1,200.

sets.title: Add and subtract measures: word problems

items.q: Oliver has 85 cm of ribbon. He cuts off 30 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means subtract: 85 − 30 = 55 cm.

items.q: Isla has two pieces of ribbon. One is 45 cm long. The other is 38 cm long. How much ribbon is there altogether?
items.e: Add: 45 + 38. 5 + 8 = 13, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten. 45 + 38 = 83 cm.

items.q: A sunflower was 35 cm tall. It grew 18 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: Add: 35 + 18 = 53 cm. Remember to exchange: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Charlie builds a train track 3 m long. He adds 1 m 50 cm more track. How long is the track now?
items.e: Add the metres: 3 m + 1 m = 4 m. Then add the 50 cm. The track is 4 m 50 cm long.

items.q: Zara is 1 m 25 cm tall. Lily is 1 m 10 cm tall. How much taller is Zara?
items.e: Both are 1 m and some more. Compare the centimetres: 25 − 10 = 15 cm.

items.q: Grace has 1 m 40 cm of string. She ties on 80 cm more. How long is the string now?
items.e: 40 cm + 80 cm = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm. Add this to 1 m: 1 m + 1 m 20 cm = 2 m 20 cm.

items.q: Alfie needs 250 g of flour for a cake and 175 g of flour for biscuits. How much flour does he need altogether?
items.e: Add: 250 + 175. 5 tens + 7 tens = 12 tens, so exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. 250 + 175 = 425 g.

items.q: Ethan has a 1 kg bag of flour. He uses 350 g to bake bread. How much flour is left?
A bag of apples weighs 600 g. A bag of oranges weighs 450 g. How much do they weigh altogether?
A parcel can weigh up to 2 kg. Mum's parcel weighs 1 kg 300 g. How much more can she put in it?
Evie's school bag weighs 2 kg. She puts in a lunchbox that weighs 500 g. How much does the bag weigh now?
items.e: Add the grams to the kilograms: 2 kg + 500 g = 2 kg 500 g.

items.q: Mohammed has a 500 ml bottle of water. He drinks 175 ml. How much water is left?
items.e: Subtract: 500 − 175. Exchange across the zeros: 500 − 175 = 325 ml. Check: 325 + 175 = 500.

items.q: A recipe needs 300 ml of milk. Leo has 1 l of milk. How much milk is left after making the recipe?
For a party, Dad buys a 1 l carton of juice and a 500 ml carton of juice. How much juice is there altogether?
items.e: Add the millilitres to the litres: 1 l + 500 ml = 1 l 500 ml (1,500 ml).

items.q: For a party, a jug holds 1 l of squash. Four cups of 200 ml are poured. How much squash is left in the jug?
At a party there are 2 l of orange juice. The children drink 1 l 400 ml. How much juice is left?
A fish tank has 5 l of water. 2 l 500 ml more is added. How much water is in the tank now?
items.e: Add the litres: 5 l + 2 l = 7 l. Then add the 500 ml: 7 l 500 ml.

items.q: Ava needs ribbon to wrap presents. She has 2 m of ribbon and uses 75 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. Subtract: 200 − 75 = 125 cm. 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.

items.q: On sports day, Ruby jumps 1 m 85 cm. Maya jumps 2 m 10 cm. How much further does Maya jump?
items.e: 1 m 85 cm = 185 cm and 2 m 10 cm = 210 cm. Count on: 185 → 200 is 15 cm, 200 → 210 is 10 cm. 15 + 10 = 25 cm.

items.q: A brown worm is 45 mm long. A pink worm is 6 cm long. Which worm is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 6 cm = 60 mm. 60 mm is more than 45 mm, so the pink worm is longer. 60 − 45 = 15 mm. Do not take 6 from 45: change to the same unit first.
